hypothesis: The failure of within-user BPR (n001-n003, best 0.5797 vs the 0.6016 pointwise anchor) says the loss/metric mismatch is not the binding constraint; the binding constraint is that user_id x video_id embeddings have no usable prior for items the user has few or no co-occurrences with, which is exactly where n003 collapses (pop_q1 = 0.357, pop_q2 = 0.446 vs pop_q4 = 0.581). I claim that a causal, past-dates-only, EB-smoothed item-side history feature (item long_view rate and item exposure count, decile-binned, computed for each date using only strictly earlier dates) carries item quality signal that varies within a user and therefore can reorder impressions, and that adding it plus a decile-binned user historical long_view rate (which is inert on its own but becomes an active user x item cross inside FM) to the FM pointwise baseline lifts validation primary by at least +0.002 above 0.6016, with the gain concentrated in the pop_q1/pop_q2 (rare-item) segments and near zero in pop_q4 where the ID embeddings are already well estimated. If primary moves less than +0.002 and the pop_q1/q2 segments do not improve, then item-side historical propensity is already absorbed by the video_id embedding and the remaining headroom is not in static-plus-aggregate features at all, redirecting the loop to sequence/multi-task representations.

I hold model class (FM), loss (pointwise, as in the n000 baseline) and seed fixed so the delta is attributable to the features alone.
